text: Last day I was there, helicopter spotted enemy outside perimeter, about 450 of them digging defensive positions. I never heard the helicopter, but anyways I told Sgt Lowery about the enemy digging and about an hour went by and he came back and said "You son of a bitch you killed 450 civilians down there!" and I knew that was wrong because i never changed my radio station. I never changed it ever. Like I can't just call up a jet to call up and attach something. Somebody up there, probably Sgt Lowery, probably reported me KIA. All the officers were gone, so he was the only one on the other radio in Special Forces that I know of. When they came and got me, captain Geutler (his spelling) came and got me and dropped off Sgt Weaver, he was a E5 specialist. He was an ex marine. So I left. I didn't work for Special Forces, i worked for 1st Cavalry. They took me back to Thon Suhn Nut (my spelling) where you see a mobile trailer and next it was a medic trailer, and said he wasn't feeling well and the guy said "No shit you have yellow jaundice" and then the next day they place me in Cholon near where the French swimming pool was at for maybe 3 days and then they flew me to Subic Bay in the Philippines and I was there 4-5 days and then they flew me to Camp Zama outside Tokyo. That's how I got medivac out. I was in and out of consciousness. I didn't know I was reported KIA at this time. In the first 3-4 days I saw the name in the KIA list and went straight to the chaplin in the hospital in Camp Zama. I told him I was KIA and I was still alive. I doubt if there was somebody with the same name.
